lines.line: Summary: In Left 4 Dead 2 versus, only the team on the survivor side scores, and most of its points come from distance. Each survivor is credited with the furthest spot they get to, so one who turns back and dies keeps the ground already covered.

quoted: Points are only awarded to teams playing as the Survivors.
The distance traveled by each Survivor is the primary source of points for the Survivors.
The farthest distance a Survivor reaches is the score that Survivor gets (i.e., if a Survivor backtracks and dies, they will receive points for how far they traveled before backtracking).

lines.line: Tips: A survivor who is alive when the chapter ends is worth 25 more points to the team, unless they die in the safe room before its door shuts. Health and carried items no longer change the score, and reviving a dead survivor with a defibrillator costs 25 points.

quoted: Every Survivor that lives at the end of the chapter gets a 25-point bonus for their team.
If the Survivor makes it into the safe room and dies before the saferoom door closes, the 25-point bonus will not count.
The health or items of the Survivors no longer affects the score.
Reviving dead Survivors using a Defibrillator results in a 25-point penalty.

lines.line: Tips: A tie where every survivor reached the safe room on both sides is settled by damage: the team whose infected players did more gets 25 bonus points. That tiebreaker does not apply when someone died, even if the scores are equal. Both sides are told whenever the survivors pass another 25% of the distance.

quoted: In the event that both teams reach the safe room with no deaths, a 25-point tiebreak bonus is given to the team who did the most damage as Infected.
If both teams earn the same score in a level, but not everyone makes it to the safe room (i.e. someone dies), this tiebreaker does not occur.
The Infected and Survivor sides are notified at 25% intervals of the distance the Survivors have traveled.

lines.line: Tips: The wiki's Tactics page tells survivors to focus on making progress rather than tracking down a Hunter, and says this matters most in versus. Its Realism Versus page adds that moving slowly and carefully can sometimes beat racing ahead when you are going for team points.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Hunter / The Survivors
quoted: your focus should be on progressing, not finding and killing the Hunter. This is especially true in Versus
sometimes moving slowly and cautiously is much better than trying to blaze ahead and get team points for the team

sections.name: Versus special infected spawn order and mixes

lines.line: Summary: When a versus infected player's wait to respawn is over, the AI Director assigns which special infected they become.

quoted: The AI Director determines which Special Infected "class" each player will spawn as once their spawn timer runs out and they enter spawn mode.

lines.line: Tips: In Left 4 Dead 2 versus, the four infected players nearly always get four different specials. The Director seldom deals out four pinners (Smoker, Charger, Hunter, Jockey), which keeps the team from pinning all four survivors in one move; Boomer and Spitter support instead of pinning.

quoted: In Left 4 Dead 2, the Infected team will almost always consist of four different Special Infected.
The Director rarely chooses a combination of four "pinning" Special Infected.
"Pinning" Infected are the Smoker, Charger, Hunter and the Jockey
This is so the Infected team cannot simply pin all four players at once, ending the round.
The Spitter and the Boomer do not pin in their attacks; instead, they play a support role to the other Infected

lines.line: Tips: The Tank is a random extra, at most one per level, and your chance of getting him rises with your score. After the sides swap, the other team usually starts with the same specials in the same places and order.

quoted: The Tank is a special spawn, randomly occurring, with a maximum of one instance per level
Control of the Tank is given to a player on the Infected team randomly, with the odds of selection increasing with the player's score.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Difficulty and Game Modes / Versus Mode
quoted: players on the infected team will usually spawn in the same locations and sequence at the enemy team did.
if the last round began with a jockey, a boomer, a smoker, and a spitter, the other team will start with the same special infected after the swap.

lines.line: Tips: With fewer than three infected players, bots fill the empty slots and the Director may spawn two of the same type, or all the bot specials at once. With four infected players the respawn wait can reach 30 seconds, about 20 on average.

quoted: in the case of less than three Infected players, two Special Infected of the same type may spawn
The Director can also spawn all of the AI Special Infected at the same time.
an update in Left 4 Dead 2 has added Special Infected bots in its Versus mode
When there are four Infected, players can wait up to 30 seconds to respawn, although the average is closer to 20 seconds.

lines.line: Summary: When the respawn timer runs out, a versus infected player becomes a ghost: the screen takes on a blue tint, and they choose where to appear. Survivors cannot see a ghost; its teammates see it outlined in blue.

quoted: the Infected player will enter spawn mode which is indicated by a blue tint on screen.
The player must choose where they want to spawn.
The Infected player cannot be seen by the Survivor team.
Other Infected see spawning players as a blue outline.

lines.line: Tips: You can appear on any clear ground at a middling distance from the survivors (not right beside them and not far off), out of their view and outside a restricted zone. The starting safe room counts as restricted until the survivors have left it.

quoted: can spawn in any unblocked space, provided that they are not too close to the Survivors or too far from them, they are not in the Survivors' line of sight, and they are not in a restricted area
the starting safe room prior to the Survivors vacating it

lines.line: Tips: A ghost can slip through doors, smashable objects and certain barricades, and nobody can damage it. Falling into a zone that kills on contact still ends it, and the respawn timer starts over just as it would after a normal death.

quoted: Unspawned "ghost" infected can move through destructible objects and physics objects, such as doors and certain barricades.
These unspawned Infected cannot be harmed by other players, either Infected or Survivor
they will be killed without spawning if they fall into instant-kill zones
Infected who "die" in ghost mode restart their spawn timer as though they had actually died

lines.line: Tips: An infected player who falls well behind the survivors is offered a jump up to the group's position, which puts them in spawn mode there. Survivors deny a spot by watching it or standing near it, and a sudden dash that puts an important spot in view before the infected player there can react and spawn can wreck an ambush, though it is risky.

quoted: When an Infected gets to far behind the Survivors, a message will appear giving the Infected the option of moving closer to the group.
By pressing this, you will be in the respawn mode at the Survivors' location.
getting a spot into you or your teammates' line of sight or close proximity, denies your opponents spawning in that location.

It is possible, although risky, to suddenly rush and get a vital location into a Survivor's line of sight before an Infected player at that location has time to react and spawn, ruining the entire ambush plan.

sections.name: Using the Witch as the infected team

lines.line: Summary: In versus nobody can be the Witch, yet she is a useful trap: a single hit from her incapacitates a survivor on any difficulty, so the infected team can work her into its plans and send survivors toward her.

quoted: You cannot play as the Witch, Common Infected, or Uncommon Infected.
On all difficulties, getting hit by a Witch will deal 100 damage, resulting in instant incapacitation.
you can use her in your tactics

lines.line: Tips: A Smoker can pull a survivor over to the Witch, and a Jockey can steer one toward her. A Spitter can protect her by spitting acid close to her; survivors hurrying out of the puddles may bump into her or end up next to her.

quoted: Smokers can drag Survivors to the Witch.
Jockeys can steer Survivors towards the Witch.
Spitters can protect the Witch by spitting acid near her.
Survivors will usually attempt to get away from the acid puddles quickly, which may cause them to touch the Witch or get near the Witch

lines.line: Tips: A Hunter or Boomer crouching in front of her blocks the survivors' view of her. If a Boomer dies while the survivors are fairly near her, the burst startles her and she goes after the one who killed it. In versus, a non-Tank infected player can also claw her once on spotting a survivor, which leaves her nearly enraged.

quoted: Hunters and Boomers can crouch in front of the Witch, obscuring her from the Survivors' sight.
if a Boomer is killed while the Survivors are relatively close to the Witch, the explosion will startle her, sending her after the person who killed the Boomer.
In Versus, non-Tank infected players can claw the Witch once upon spotting a Survivor, upon which she becomes near enraged.

lines.line: Tips: Skilled Hunters tend to wait, crouched and out of view, near the Witch; when a survivor rushes in to hit her, they leap on that survivor just before he can shoot. If a Hunter pounces on a survivor the Witch has already downed and is attacking, the Hunter takes no damage and the survivor dies twice as quickly. The infected see a calm Witch outlined in white, and the outline shifts toward red as she gets closer to being startled.

quoted: Experienced Hunter players normally crouch just out of sight near the Witch, waiting until a player runs up to attack the Witch and pouncing them just before they get a chance to fire.
If you pounce a Survivor as a Hunter while the Witch has already incapacitated someone and is attacking, you will not be damaged, and the Survivor will die twice as fast.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Players / Infected / Controls of the Infected
quoted: Docile Witches will have a white outline.
Witches in the process of being startled will have an outline that slowly changes from white to red

sections.name: Answering combined special attacks in versus

lines.line: Summary: How versus survivors answer the infected team's bile and the grabs that follow: spread out enough that one burst cannot catch everyone, hold fire while blinded, stay close together, and break a grab quickly.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Boomer / The Survivors
quoted: Avoid being too bunched up with the other Survivors.
Hold your fire! Since you can't see, friendly fire is the most likely result. Shove instead

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Smoker / The Survivors
quoted: When you or one of your teammates hear a Smoker, stay close together and watch out for each other.
simply shove the Survivor free or shoot the tongue

lines.line: Tips: Do not stand too close together when a Boomer is around, so a single burst of bile cannot cover all four survivors. If he gets near, shove him back and retreat before firing, and only shoot once he is well clear of you and your teammates.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Boomer / The Survivors
quoted: Avoid being too bunched up with the other Survivors.
There's no sense in all four of you getting puked on at once.
If the Boomer is too close, it's a good idea to melee-shove them, which will push them back to some degree, then back away to a safe distance before shooting
Only if the Boomer is sufficiently far away from both yourself and all other Survivors should you shoot them.

lines.line: Tips: While you are covered in bile you cannot see, so shooting is likely to hit a teammate; shove instead and head for the nearest corner you can defend. The others should stay near the biled survivor, and a thrown pipe bomb can distract the horde.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Boomer / The Survivors
quoted: Hold your fire! Since you can't see, friendly fire is the most likely result. Shove instead
Immediately find the nearest defensible corner
Stay close to the stricken Survivor.
Throw a pipe bomb to distract the horde

lines.line: Tips: A survivor who is alone and far from the group is an easy target for a Smoker, so keep close together when you hear one. A grabbed survivor has only a few seconds to shoot their way free.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Smoker / The Survivors
quoted: If any of the Survivors are alone and too far away from the group, they make an easy target for the Smoker.
When a Smoker grabs you, you will have a few seconds to free yourself by shooting the Smoker.

lines.line: Summary: A Charger that sweeps survivors over a high drop can incapacitate or kill them, and the wiki calls his charge deadly near cliffs and ledges.

quoted: Your charge is deadly near ledges and cliffs.
Avoid situations where the Charger can knock other Survivors off a high ledge, as it will either kill or incapacitate them.
If there's an area where there's a long drop or lethal area with no boundaries (such as a cliff or the top of a building), you should attempt to charge someone off

lines.line: Tips: As the Charger, ambush instead of charging from far off, because a long run gives survivors time to react and dodge. You can start a charge from a raised spot without stopping first. A survivor clipped sideways beside a high drop may be left hanging and incapacitated, and one sent far enough past the edge may plunge to their death.

quoted: Avoid charges from a long distance. The Survivors will react quickly enough to dodge you
Ambushes will maximize your chance at successfully charging an enemy.
Chargers can begin their charge from a high place without stopping.
Survivors that are knocked aside might be incapacitated by hanging if they are close to a high ledge when they are hit.
if they are knocked far enough past the ledge, they may fall to their deaths.

lines.line: Tips: Survivors should not jump away from an oncoming Charger, since even a small drop in height can cause heavy fall damage or sudden death. Bots never attempt to avoid a charge, so keep them well away from him. Melee shoves have no effect, as he is immune to them; only explosives stumble him, and the grenade launcher is the one explosive that does not.

quoted: never try to jump when a Charger is charging. Even a slight height difference can result in catastrophic fall damage or even instant death.
Bots do not make any attempt to dodge a Charger's charge, so keep them away from the Charger if one is present.
The Charger is completely immune to melee shoves, so don't try to shove him.
only explosives
other than the Grenade Launcher
will work in stumbling him.

lines.line: Summary: In versus, when a Hunter pins someone or a Jockey jumps on one, survivors standing nearby are thrown back, and in some places that leaves them dangling from a ledge. Stay a little apart, just far enough that the knockback does not reach your teammates.

quoted: On Versus and Survival modes, the Hunter's pounce will generate knockback to nearby Survivors if it manages to pin someone. Try to stay away from each other, just to the point where the Hunter won't knockback nearby Survivors if he grabs someone.

On Versus and Survival, if a Jockey jumps on someone, nearby Survivors will be knocked back, similar to a Hunter pouncing a Survivor with others nearby. In some areas, this can cause Survivors to hang onto a ledge.

lines.line: Tips: Stay near at least one teammate. A crouching Hunter gives off a telltale growl just before he leaps; when you hear it, warn the other survivors. Hunters in versus, and on harder difficulties, tend to claw rather than leap, so a survivor whose health meter falls oddly fast is probably being attacked by one close by.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Hunter / The Survivors
quoted: Always have at least one buddy close at hand.
Listen for the distinctive growl the Hunter makes when he is crouched and ready to pounce.
Once you hear the cues, remind the other Survivors of the Hunter's presence
On higher difficulties, and in Versus, the Hunter will often use their claw attack instead of pouncing the Survivors.
If someone's health meter drops unusually fast, it is usually an indicator that a Hunter is attacking nearby.

lines.line: Tips: Against a Jockey, a melee shove knocks him off and stuns him, which gives you time to shoot. Moving constantly makes you harder to land on. If one is already riding you, steer against the direction he is pulling; that leaves you moving very slowly and gives teammates time to knock him off. When hazards like fire are close, deal with the Jockeys first.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Jockey / The Survivors
quoted: Use melee shove to knock Jockeys off. They will be stunned so you can shoot them.
Keep moving so you are a difficult target to pounce on.
Move in the opposite direction of where the Jockey is steering you. This will make you move extremely slowly, allowing teammates to come and knock the Jockey off.
prioritize Jockeys if there are any hazards nearby, such as fire

lines.line: Summary: In versus a Smoker hurts his victim while pulling them along. A Spitter has little health, so any weapon can drop her in a handful of shots.

quoted: The Smoker now deals damage when he is dragging the Survivor.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Spitter / The Survivors
quoted: A Spitter does not have a lot of health, so a few shots from any weapon can kill her instantly.

lines.line: Tips: A Smoker usually attacks from behind you or from higher ground, though a few appear ahead of you. A grabbed teammate can be freed by killing the Smoker, shoving him, or breaking the tongue; a cut tongue regrows slowly and can strike again after about 15 seconds.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Smoker / The Survivors
quoted: Smokers tend to attack from behind or above your location, but some will spawn in front of you
Survivors can be rescued by killing/shoving the Smoker, or by attacking and breaking the tongue.
The Smoker's tongue will slowly grow back after being cut off and can be used to attack again after around 15 seconds.

lines.line: Tips: At long range, either a Hunting Rifle or a Sniper Rifle deals with a Spitter easily. When she dies she leaves a puddle of acid, a small one; hold back until it has gone, since neither detouring around it nor jumping over it works.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Spitter / The Survivors
quoted: Using a Hunting Rifle or a Sniper Rifle should take care of her easily at long range.
When the Spitter dies, she will leave a small pool of acid around her corpse.
Wait for the acid to disappear before moving further down.
Never try to go around a Spitter's acid
Jumping does not work either.

lines.line: Tips: In a tight hallway, a versus Spitter that cannot hit survivors directly will spit across their route. They either push through the acid and get hurt, or hold back until it is gone, and holding back gives the Spitter's teammates time to respawn.

quoted: If you are for some reason unable to spit on the Survivors directly in a tight hallway on Versus, spit in their path.
They will have two choices: Go through the acid and take damage, or wait until it disappears. If they choose to wait, this will allow your teammates time to respawn.

lines.line: Summary: A versus Tank starts with 6000 health. As soon as the survivors walk into the area the Director picked for him, an infected player takes him over, and he is aggressive from the first moment.

quoted: The Tank has 6000 health points. The Director will also spawn them on the map when the Survivors enter a designed area, and let an Infected player take control immediately
The Tank is immediately aggressive

lines.line: Tips: Fire does more good than explosives: setting him alight with a Molotov or gas can keeps hurting him over time, though in versus burning no longer slows him down.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Tank / The Survivors
quoted: Set the Tank on fire by using either a molotov or a gas can.
great for limited big damage, but not as effective as fire, which always does guaranteed damage over time to the Tank
this loss of speed from fire in Versus was removed by patches in both games in October 2010

lines.line: Tips: Stay away from the Tank whenever you can, and never let him trap you in a corner, since there is nowhere to go and you will probably be taken down.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Tank / The Survivors
quoted: Keep your distance from the Tank if at all possible.
Never let the Tank back you into a corner as you can't go anywhere, and most likely you will be taken down.

lines.line: Tips: When he is beating on a downed teammate, a survivor who shoves him or strikes him from behind can draw his attention away; shooting him does not do that. Any melee weapon deals 500 damage per swing, and explosives deal about 750.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Tank / The Survivors
quoted: another Survivor can aggravate the Tank and possibly draw its attention from its target by shoving and hitting it in the back.
Shooting a Tank won't have the same effect
Melee weapons deal 500 damage per swing at the Tank, regardless of what type.
Explosives deal around 750 damage to the Tank.

lines.line: Summary: Coordinating their attacks is the most important thing for the infected side, according to the wiki: a Hunter pouncing alone is shot down before he does much harm, and a Smoker's catch gets freed with little trouble.

quoted: Coordinating Your Attacks:
This is by far the most important factor in a Left 4 Dead Versus match.
If a Hunter pounces on his own, he will just get killed before he can do any real damage.
If a Smoker tries to constrict a Survivor they will just get freed without any real effort

lines.line: Tips: The Boomer should lead off, covering as many survivors in bile as possible. The Hunters then spring out of their hiding places and the Smoker pulls one survivor away. Should the bile land on a single survivor, go for the other three, who are clean, with pounces and the Smoker.

quoted: The best tactic for coordinating your attacks is to let the Boomer vomit on as many people as he can.
Then, have the Hunters pounce from their hiding spots and make the Smoker pull someone away.
If the Boomer vomits on one person, then pounce or constrict the other three who haven't got Boomer bile on them!

lines.line: Tips: A Smoker that drags someone through a horde leaves a gap, and a Charger can use that gap to frighten off the survivors rushing to help. A Spitter should follow another special and spit on a survivor it has just pinned, particularly a Charger's or Hunter's. A Charger also does well to attack right after bile lands, picking survivors with no bile on them.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Smoker / The Infected
quoted: Smokers can drag a Survivor through a horde, creating a passage. The same passage can be used by a Charger to scare off the Survivors who rush to help their ensnared ally.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Spitter / The Infected
quoted: follow an another attacker Special Infected and immediately spit over a survivor they've just pinned especially from the likes of a Charger or Hunter
Attacking when Boomer bile has just covered the Survivors is a useful tactic. Aim for the Survivors who aren't covered

lines.line: Tips: As a rule, the Boomer belongs out in front of the survivors, where he can lie in wait, and the Smoker behind them, where he can drag someone back; Hunters stay close to one of the two and exploit the confusion they cause. Hunters also do much better with something in front of them, such as the horde, a Charger or a Tank.

quoted: In general, the Boomer should spawn ahead of the Survivors so he can properly ambush while the Smoker should spawn behind to pull someone back. Hunters should be near the Smoker or the Boomer

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Hunter / The Infected
quoted: Hunters work significantly better with a meat shield (the horde, Charger, Tank).

lines.line: Summary: Charger ambush spots for the infected team on the first three chapters of Dead Center, The Hotel, The Streets and The Mall. Chargers do best on survivors squeezed into a narrow spot, lined up or bunched together.

quoted: always attack Survivors that are in a narrow area, in a straight line, or otherwise tight clump.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dead Center
quoted: The Hotel
The Streets
The Mall

lines.line: Tips: The Hotel: charge a survivor standing beside a window with no railing on its ledge and they fall to their death. Try to pin someone in the fire lying between the lobby and the kitchen; it hurts far more than usual, and teammates reviving the downed survivor take heavy damage from it too.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dead Center
quoted: If a Survivor is by a window that doesn't have a railing on the ledge, charge at them, and you should bring the Survivor to their death.
try to pin them in the fire.
The fire between the kitchen and the main lobby does significantly increased damage
Teammates that are reviving the incapacitated Survivor will take massive damage from the fire as well

lines.line: Tips: The Streets: haul one survivor a long way from his teammates. The path leading up to the gun store is a long straight run, with little space for survivors to dodge. When they are on the ladder up the dumpster, climb up yourself and charge; this normally knocks every one of them back.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dead Center
quoted: The best you can do is try to carry a Survivor far away from the group.
Before the gun store, there is a long straight path to charge the Survivors with little room of dodging.
While the Survivors climb a ladder on the dumpster, climb up and charge at them; this will usually knock all of them back.

lines.line: Tips: The Mall: take survivors over the edge of the upper floors. On an escalator, wait until all of them are riding it, then drive through the whole line the instant the front one reaches the far end; those sent flying may take fall damage.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dead Center
quoted: Try to carry the Survivors off of the higher floors.
Wait for all of them to start going up/down, and as soon as the first Survivor reaches the end of the escalator, charge straight into the escalator and through all of them.
The teammates who are sent flying might receive fall damage.

lines.line: Summary: Charger ambush spots for the infected team on the first four chapters of Dark Carnival: The Highway, The Fairgrounds, The Coaster and The Barns.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dark Carnival
quoted: The Highway
The Fairgrounds
The Coaster
The Barns

lines.line: Tips: The Highway: in the motel, grab a survivor on the upper walkway and pull them off it, which delays and hurts them. Charge whoever is at the back just before the group leaps down the slope toward the swamp, and the victim is stranded and eventually dies. Toward the finish of the level you can also drive a survivor right back down that slope.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dark Carnival
quoted: In the motel, try to grab a Survivor that is on the upper walkway. Pull them off to delay and damage them.
Charging the last Survivor before they can jump down the hill into the swamp will cause your victim to be stranded and will eventually perish.
Charge a Survivor all the way back down the hill near the end of the level.

lines.line: Tips: The Fairgrounds: once the survivors have climbed the building past Kiddie Land, a ramp sits behind the ladder, and you can charge them down it back toward Kiddie Land, which costs them a large amount of time or one of their team.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dark Carnival
quoted: When the Survivors climb to the top of the building after Kiddie Land, there is a ramp behind the ladder that makes it possible to charge them back into Kiddie Land; this either makes them lose a lot of time or a fellow Survivor.

lines.line: Tips: The Coaster: just as the survivors step out of the safe room by the Tunnel of Love and climb the stairs, come at them from the far side of the staircase and smash the lot of them against the wall. A variation is to spawn inside the safe room and charge toward the tunnel from the other direction, because the survivors are expecting a charge to come out of the tunnel.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dark Carnival
quoted: At the start of the Tunnel of Love, when the Survivors open the safe room door and go up the stairs, charge from the opposite side of the stairs, slamming all of them into the wall
A good variation on this is to spawn in the safe room, charge from the opposite direction towards the tunnel, because everyone is expecting a charge from the tunnel.

lines.line: Tips: The Barns: rooftops make a great spot to send survivors over the side. Survivors often line up in the long alley after the Crescendo Event, and concealing yourself in a crowd of common infected helps with that.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dark Carnival
quoted: The rooftops are a great place to charge Survivors off of.
survivors will often line up and allow you to bowl through them. Hiding in the swarms of Common Infected can make this easier

lines.line: Summary: Charger ambush spots for the infected team on the first three chapters of Swamp Fever: Plank Country, The Swamp and Shanty Town.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Swamp Fever
quoted: The Plank Country
The Swamp
Shanty Town

lines.line: Tips: Plank Country: when the survivors stand on the dock ahead of the Crescendo Event, seize one or, better still, send one tumbling into deep water; the one you grabbed and any you struck die at once. The same trick works when they step off the ferry on the far side of the map: wait behind a tree, then charge one of them off the dock. On the walkways, getting them to drop into the swamp slows them down a lot.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Swamp Fever
quoted: When the Survivors are on the dock right before the Crescendo Event, try to grab, or better yet, knock one into the deep water. This will kill the Survivor you grabbed and the ones you hit instantly.
as soon as they exit the ferry at the other side of the map. Hide behind one of the trees then attempt to ambush and charge one of the survivors off the dock.
while the Survivors are on the walkways, try to get them to fall down into the swamp. This will slow them down considerably.

lines.line: Tips: The Swamp: dunking survivors in the water pays off, since their whole team is slowed.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Swamp Fever
quoted: Taking the Survivors into the water is useful because their team will be slowed down by the water.

lines.line: Tips: Shanty Town: you are not slowed by the water as the survivors are, so go after a survivor who is on their own. There are also a few cramped places to dash in and strike with a melee attack.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Swamp Fever
quoted: The water will slow down Survivors, but not you. Use this to charge lone Survivors.
There are a few tight points that you can rush in and use your melee attack.

lines.line: Summary: Survival is a mode in both Left 4 Dead games: wave after wave of infected keeps coming until every survivor is dead or incapacitated. It cannot be won; the aim is to last as long as possible and set records.

quoted: This game mode throws waves and waves of the Infected at the Survivors until they get fully overwhelmed via every survivor dying or getting incapacitated.
There is no way to win, as instead the goal is to survive as long as you can and set new records.
Survival mode gameplay in Left 4 Dead 2 remains similar to Left 4 Dead's survival mode

lines.line: Tips: Before you start the horde, gather as many supplies as you can and settle on the best spot. Set up the special ammo, and put gas cans or propane tanks somewhere secure, so the team can grab them quickly in a Tank attack when no Molotovs are in hand.

quoted: It is always best to hole up by gathering as much resources and finding the best spot possible before setting off the Horde.
preparing special ammo boxes and placing Gas Cans/Propane Tanks in a secure spot can allow the team to grab it quickly in the event of a Tank attack if they do not have any Molotovs on hand
Place everything you need in the place you plan to hold out in, so you do not have to leave your area for supplies and risk getting attacked easily.

lines.line: Tips: To choose where to hold out, check the ammo and supplies nearby, the entrances, escape routes, high ground and how far you can see. Aim for just one or two ways in, so that two survivors can cover each of them.

quoted: Ammunition:
Supplies:
Points of Entry:
Escape Routes:
High Ground:
Line of Sight:
Try to keep the number of entry points down to two or one, if possible, so that at least two survivors are covering each entrance.

lines.line: Tips: The wiki's Survival tips give steady times for Tanks and hordes within the first 12 minutes: the first Tank at 0:40, and two together at both 5:30 and 11:30. New common-infected hordes stop for roughly 3:50 to 4:25, 9:00 to 9:35 and 12:00 to 12:30; only special infected can appear then, which makes those windows good for healing or an ammo run.

quoted: Tanks and hordes spawn at consistent times during the first 12 minutes.
Tanks will consistently spawn at 0:40,
Take note of the double Tank spawns at 5:30 and 11:30

New hordes of common infected do not spawn from approximately 3:50-4:25, 9:00-9:35, and 12:00-12:30; this means that, during those times, the only infected that can spawn are Special Infected, making those times ideal for ammo runs, healing, or other actions that would be risky otherwise.

lines.line: Summary: Realism Versus is ordinary versus with the same scoring, but the survivor side plays under Realism rules, which make common infected tougher and let a Witch kill with a single hit.

quoted: Realism Versus follows normal rules for Versus in terms of gameplay style and scoring, but makes things harder for the Survivors as they are bound by Realism rules.
Common Infected are tougher, there are no glows around Survivors or items, and the Witch can kill in one hit

lines.line: Tips: As a survivor, never go off alone: if you are in trouble away from the group, your teammates will probably not get to you in time. A Hunter's growl and a Smoker's cough are the sounds to catch; call them out when you hear them. Talk through a microphone rather than typing, since typing leaves you unable to defend yourself. Resist the pull of the top-tier special weapons such as the Grenade Launcher or M60 when you can; smart infected will sit on those spots and ambush whoever turns up.

quoted: Never run off. Ever.
since visibility through walls is removed, teammates will probably never make it to the ailing player in time.
Listen carefully for the growl of a Hunter, or the cough of a Smoker.
It's highly recommended to use a microphone to communicate with the teammates as typing with a keyboard always renders the Survivor vulnerable to any Infected attack.
Don't rush off for the Special Tier weapons like the Grenade Launcher or M60 if you can help it
if the Special Infected get smart, they'll camp those spots and wait for players to run into the ambush.

lines.line: Tips: Playing the infected, a survivor on their own is an easy kill. Camp spots where tier 2 weapons lie or healing supplies can be plainly seen, since survivors very often run to them. Infected hit harder in this mode, so even a few hits from a Charger can badly hurt the team. A Jockey can put any survivor down, whatever their health, because teammates first have to find the victim before they can shove him off.

quoted: Lone Survivors are always easy fodder.
Try to camp Tier 2 weapon locations or spots with clearly visible healing supplies, as the chances of Survivors rushing to those spots are extremely high.
Infected damage is increased here so even if a player only gets in a couple of hits as a Charger, the attack could cripple their team greatly.
in Realism Versus, a Jockey can easily incapacitate a Survivor regardless of health, since the other players first need to find the victim to shove the Jockey off.

lines.line: Tips: Infected players still see survivor auras as usual, except that the Tank cannot see the red auras on cars and other objects he could throw at survivors. Realism Versus later lost every defibrillator to a patch, along with every first aid kit except the starting kits survivors are given at the beginning of a map.

quoted: Players on the Infected team will still see auras normally, except that the Tank will not see red auras around cars and other objects that he can punch at the Survivors.
A later patch removed all Defibrillators from Realism Versus, as well as all First aid kits other than the ones that the Survivors begin each map with.

sections.name: Versus rounds, turns and who plays survivors first

lines.line: Summary: In versus a round is two turns: one team plays the survivors, the other plays the infected, and then the sides swap. Each team has up to four players, and only the team on the survivor side earns points.

quoted: Two separate teams of 4 players take turns playing as the Survivors and the Infected, competing for the most points.
Points are only awarded to teams playing as the Survivors.
Each Round of a versus game consists of two turns.

lines.line: Tips: Before the game starts, whoever leads the lobby picks the campaign, and each player chooses whether to start on the infected side or the survivor side.

quoted: Before a game starts, the lobby leader chooses a specific campaign to play and the players can choose which team to play on by choosing whether to start as Infected or Survivors.

lines.line: Tips: A turn as survivors ends the moment they reach the end of the chapter, or when all of them are incapacitated or dead. Then the sides swap, and once both turns are done everyone sees the current team scores.

quoted: The teams switch sides as soon as the Survivors reach the end or they are all incapacitated or killed.
At the end of each round, all players see their current team scores.

lines.line: Tips: In the next round, the team with the higher score plays the survivors first. After a tie, the team that was survivors first in the previous round goes first again. Versus is played on Normal difficulty.

quoted: After a chapter end for both teams, whichever team currently has the highest score will play as Survivors first in the next round. In the event of a tie, the team that played the Survivors first for the previous round will play them first again in the next.
Versus games are played on Normal difficulty.

sections.name: Versus chapters repeat for both teams

lines.line: Summary: Every chapter is played twice, once by each team, so the second team to play it finds the items in the same places and the Tank and Witch in similar ones.

quoted: Since each chapter of a campaign is played through twice (once for both teams)

weapons, healing items, and other objects will spawn in exactly the same place for both teams when they play as Survivors, and the Witch and the Tank will usually spawn in similar places for both teams, though slight variation does occur

lines.line: Tips: Survivors start each chapter without the weapons, health, gnomes or items they held on the previous map, and the first couple of chapters hand out tier 1 weapons. Safe-room items used in the previous round come back.

quoted: they will not retain any weapons, health, gnomes, or items from the previous map, and they will begin with Tier 1 weapons at the beginning couple of chapters
Items from the safe room that were used during the previous round are respawned as well.

lines.line: Tips: A dead survivor does not return from a rescue closet as in the campaign. In Left 4 Dead 2 the only way back is a defibrillator, which costs the team 25 points.

quoted: Survivors do not respawn in Rescue Closets when they die, unlike the Campaign mode.
a dead Survivor can be brought back to life if another Survivor happens to have a Defibrillator; this results in a Defibrillator penalty of -25 points the team's score.

lines.line: Tips: Some maps are trimmed for versus: closets and other places where survivors could hold out for ever are removed, so the route is harder on the survivor side.

quoted: Some maps are also slightly changed to make it harder for the Survivors, such as removing closets or areas where Survivors can hold out for an indefinite amount of time.

sections.name: Survivor outline colours the infected see

lines.line: Summary: A versus infected player sees survivors as coloured outlines, and in Left 4 Dead 2 the colour shows how hurt they are: green when healthy, then yellow, orange and red as health falls.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Players / Infected / Controls of the Infected
quoted: Survivors who have health over 40 (permanent and temporary) will have a green outline.
Survivors in Left 4 Dead 2 who have health lower than 25 will have an orange outline.

lines.line: Tips: The bands count permanent and temporary health together. Over 40 is green, 25 to 39 is yellow, under 25 is orange, and under 10 or incapacitated is red. A survivor at exactly 1 health after being incapacitated, without healing, also shows red.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Players / Infected / Controls of the Infected
quoted: Survivors who have health over 40 (permanent and temporary) will have a green outline.
Survivors who have health between 10 and 39 (permanent and temporary) will have a yellow outline (between 25 and 39 health in Left 4 Dead 2).
Survivors in Left 4 Dead 2 who have health lower than 25 will have an orange outline.
Survivors who have health lower than 10 (permanent and temporary) or incapacitated will have a red outline.
Survivors in Left 4 Dead 2 who have exactly 1 health after being incapacitated without healing or are currently incapacitated will have a red outline.

lines.line: Tips: A survivor covered in Boomer bile shows purple whatever their health, and infected teammates show blue, spawned or not.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Players / Infected / Controls of the Infected
quoted: Survivors who are covered in boomer bile, regardless of their health, will have a purple outline.
Infected Teammates, spawned or not, will have a blue outline.

sections.name: What gives a versus survivor away to the infected

lines.line: Summary: The infected only see a survivor's outline after that survivor has done something noisy or open. Standing still, walking or crouch-walking stays hidden, unless an infected player has the survivor in sight or the survivor is covered in bile.

quoted: In Versus mode, if you are not firing a weapon or shoving and you are either crouch-walking, walking or standing still, your outline will not be seen by the enemy Infected.
Note that this will not apply to Survivors in sight of Infected players or Survivors covered in Boomer bile.

lines.line: Tips: These show the outline: firing a weapon, swinging or shoving, using consumables, moving without crouching or holding the walk key, being pinned, ridden or covered in bile, and being under attack.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Players / Infected / Controls of the Infected
quoted: The outline will appear when Survivors have recently performed these actions:
Shooting with any weapon.
Using their melee weapon.
Using their Melee shove.
Using consumable items.
Moving without crouching or holding the walk key.
Being pinned, constricted, pummeled, ridden, or covered in boomer bile.
Under attack.

lines.line: Tips: Voice gives you away too: using a microphone, talking, or a typed chatter-box message while the box is open. A survivor at low health keeps commenting on it, which shows their location as well.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Players / Infected / Controls of the Infected
quoted: Using a microphone.
Talking - either by scenario, interaction with the environment or Infected, or voice command.
Using the chatter box.
Note that the outline will appear once the box is active and will last until the message is sent.
Note that when Survivors are low on health, they will constantly comment about their health condition and give away their location.

lines.line: Tips: These stay hidden: reloading (though a survivor may call it out), jumping (moving sideways in the air still shows you), moving while crouched or walking, opening or closing doors, picking up or throwing items (they may shout what they hold), and starting a Crescendo event. The infected team does not share what each member can see.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Players / Infected / Controls of the Infected
quoted: Reloading; however, Survivors will sometimes yell out
Jumping.
Note that moving horizontally mid air without crouching or holding the walk key will still give away their location.
Moving while crouching or holding the walk key.
Opening or closing doors.
Picking up, releasing, or throwing items.
Starting a Crescendo event
Staying in sight of a Special Infected; the Infected team does not share their vision of Survivors.

sections.name: How special infected attacks differ when people play them

lines.line: Summary: When a person controls a special infected in versus, some attacks work differently from the campaign: the Boomer's bile can arc, the Hunter's pounce does damage, the Smoker hurts while dragging, and the Jockey's leap stuns.

quoted: Some of the Special Infected also have different attacking mechanics from Campaign mode in Normal:
The Smoker now deals damage when he is dragging the Survivor.
The Jockey's leap can also stun the Survivors just like the Hunter's pounce.

lines.line: Tips: A versus Boomer can aim upward so his bile lobs over a distance, even from a spot the survivors cannot see, and can re-aim while it is still coming out to catch anyone he missed.

quoted: The Boomer can aim upward to let the puke fly in an arc, splashing the Survivors from a further place, sometimes even from where the Survivors cannot see him.
He can also move his aiming reticule mid-puke to alter the trajectory of the outbound puke; doing so can let him hit Survivors who he had initially missed.

lines.line: Tips: A versus Hunter's pounce deals damage that grows with the length of the jump, up to 25, and stumbles survivors standing nearby. Chaining wall jumps gets him higher, but then he cannot jump away at once when attacked.

quoted: the further they jump into the air, the more damage they do when they hit (up to a 25-point maximum).
The pounce will also stumble nearby Survivors.
Experienced players can also do multiple wall jumps to attack the Survivor from higher positions; however, they lose the ability to jump away instantly when being attacked.

lines.line: Tips: A human-controlled special infected attacks the moment it spots a survivor, with none of the delay a bot has, and can spawn in the starting safe room once the survivors have left it.

quoted: As human-controlled Special Infected, there is no delay when spotting a Survivor to attack them.
AI-controlled Special Infected will still have their attacks delayed.
can spawn in the starting safe room provided that the Survivors vacate it

lines.line: Summary: A versus game can run with as few as two players, one per team, because bots fill the empty infected and survivor slots. Both teams still need at least one human or the game ends.

quoted: so now it is possible to have very few players (two players minimum, one on each team), while bots on both teams fill in the missing player slots
Both teams need at least one human player in order for the game to start or continue properly

lines.line: Tips: A team short on humans is at a real disadvantage as survivors. If every human survivor is killed the round ends, because the computer-controlled survivors cannot get through a level alone.

quoted: A team short on players can face a significant disadvantage during the game while playing as Survivors.
If all human-controlled Survivors are killed, the round will end, since the computer-controlled Survivors cannot continue through the level by themselves.

lines.line: Tips: The bots playing Ellis and Zoey reach for shotguns in versus instead of the hunting or sniper rifles they take in the campaign, for balance.

quoted: they instead take shotguns in Versus (and Survival) mode for balancing reasons.
usually take the Hunting Rifle and Sniper Rifle in campaign mode

lines.line: Tips: A bot-controlled Hunter shot from a distance cannot leap away as it does in the campaign, so it runs instead and is easy to kill. Its pounce still hurts, up to 25 damage when it starts far enough off.

quoted: Since the jump ability is not available in Versus, he will simply run away, making him an easy kill.
Up to 25 points of damage can be dealt instantly if the pounce originated far enough away.

sections.name: Fooling the infected team at ambush spots

lines.line: Summary: In versus the infected are people, so survivors can bluff them. Stopping short or backing away as you near a likely ambush spot can draw an infected player into spawning or attacking too early.

quoted: Keep in mind that the enemies are human players, and use specific strategies against them.
A common trick is the Survivor suddenly stops or back away while approaching supposed ambush spots, such as a corner, a one way drop, or a Witch.

lines.line: Tips: Think the way the infected team would. The wiki's examples of bait spots are a corner, a one-way drop and a Witch. If the bluff works, the survivors can kill the early attacker more safely, or rush past while the infected player's special attack is still recharging.

quoted: In Versus mode, think as the infected team would think.
This can easily trick the enemy team to spawn or attack too early, allowing the team to dispose of them more safely, or rush through while their special attack is still in cooldown.

lines.line: Tips: Walking or crouch-walking toward a place where a special infected probably hides keeps your outline hidden while you are not firing or shoving, which suits sneaking up on it. It does not help a survivor already in an infected player's sight or covered in bile.

quoted: This is very useful for sneaking up on a position where a Special Infected is likely to be hiding.
Note that this will not apply to Survivors in sight of Infected players or Survivors covered in Boomer bile.

lines.line: Tips: Coordinating by microphone lets a team keep several spawn spots under watch until it has passed them, which forces the opponents to wait or take a weaker spot.

quoted: With good coordination via microphone, a survivor team can keep locations where enemies can spawn for good advantages in check until they get pass, forcing the opponents to either delay their attack or choose an inferior location.

sections.name: Survivor weapons for versus: the mix and the Grenade Launcher

lines.line: Summary: The wiki advises a survivor team to carry a mix of close-range and long-range weapons rather than four of the same kind, and to treat the Grenade Launcher as a short-term pick in versus.

quoted: A team with all shotguns or all sniper rifles is far less balanced than one with a good mix of armaments.
Left 4 Dead 2's Grenade Launcher is not very useful on most maps when playing in Versus mode.

lines.line: Tips: Ideally each player carries something that hits both near and far. One example mix is a sniper rifle with a melee weapon, an assault rifle with a melee weapon, an assault rifle with two pistols, and a shotgun with a magnum.

quoted: It is best for your team to have a mix of close- and far-quarters weapons, and ideally each team member will have something that is capable of hitting both near and far targets.
an effective mix might be one sniper rifle/melee, one assault rifle/melee, one assault rifle/2 pistol, and one shotgun/magnum (for example).

lines.line: Tips: Mix the throwables too. Pipe bombs suit horde attacks, a survivor covered in bile, or clearing wide open ground; bile bombs slow a Tank or pull common infected away from the team.

quoted: Try to have a good mix of pipebombs, bile bombs, and molotovs.
Use the pipe bomb during horde attacks, when a survivor has been vomited on, or to clear out large open areas so the team can move faster.
Use bile to slow down a tank, draw common infected away from players

lines.line: Tips: The Grenade Launcher's aim is shaky, its reload slow, its ammo scarce and its friendly-fire risk high. In versus the wiki says to use it briefly during a panic event, then swap to something less likely to hurt teammates.

quoted: Its accuracy is dubious, the reloading is slow, the ammo is limited, and the potential for friendly fire damage is high.
best used temporarily during a panic event
swapped out for something that makes less collateral damage

lines.line: Summary: Scavenge is a Left 4 Dead 2 team mode: survivors haul up to 22 gas cans to a generator while player-controlled special infected try to stop them. A game is 1, 3 or 5 rounds, and each round has two turns with the sides swapping.

quoted: Scavenge Mode is a competitive gameplay mode released in Left 4 Dead 2. It is a round-based game in which Survivors attempt to find up to 22 gas cans to refuel a generator (or car), while fighting against player-controlled Special Infected much like in a Versus game.
Before a game starts, the host can choose the amount of rounds to play (1 round, 3 rounds, 5 rounds).
Each round of a game consists of two turns.

lines.line: Tips: Survivors start next to the generator with 30 seconds to set up and grab supplies. The infected spawn when that time runs out or a survivor leaves the area around the generator. Then survivors have 1 minute 30 seconds, plus 20 seconds for every can they bring to the generator.

quoted: At the start of a round, the Survivors spawn next to the generator and will have 30 seconds to set up and grab their supplies, while the Infected find locations to spawn.
The timer will start and the Infected will spawn as soon as the set-up time runs out or if a Survivor leaves the designated area around the generator.
Once the game starts, the Survivors have 1 minute and 30 seconds to find gas cans, with an additional 20 seconds added for each can they bring to the generator.

lines.line: Tips: To win a round the second team must collect one more can than the first. Equal cans go to the faster team, and if neither team gets a can the round goes to the team that lasted longer. The game ends as soon as the trailing team cannot catch up, so a 3-round game ends at two round wins.

quoted: Next turn, the previously Infected will become the Survivors and will have to get one more gas can than the other team to win the round and end it.
If both teams collect the same amount of gas cans, the team that did it faster wins the round.
In the case that both teams do not collect any gas cans, the round goes to the team who held out longer.
The game will end as soon as it is impossible for the losing team to win.

lines.line: Tips: The losing team starts the next round as survivors, the opposite of versus, where the losing team is the infected first. Most round wins takes the game, so a team can win with fewer cans overall.

quoted: Next round, the losing team will start as the Survivors (the opposite of Versus, in which the losing team is Infected first).
The team that wins the most rounds wins the game.
In other words, a team can win even if, overall, they collected fewer gas cans than their opponents as long as they win more rounds.

sections.name: Scavenge gas cans, pouring and overtime

lines.line: Summary: Scavenge gas cans always spawn in the same places and glow white, turning orange once picked up and dropped. Pouring one into the generator takes about 2.5 seconds, and any damage from the infected or from fire restarts it; friendly fire does not.

quoted: Gas cans have a white aura, so Survivors can see them anywhere on the map. If they are picked up and dropped they will have an orange aura. Gas cans always spawn in the same location on the map.

It takes about 2.5 seconds to pour fuel into the generator. However, any damage from Infected or from fire will instantly restart the pour timer (friendly fire will not), so a Survivor must not be under attack in order to complete the process.

lines.line: Tips: Only the Spitter can destroy a can with an attack, and only one that has been picked up and dropped before. A can hit by acid flashes and then explodes, which gives survivors a moment to grab it. A destroyed can eventually respawns where it started.

quoted: The only Infected that can destroy gas cans with its attack is the Spitter. However, the attack only works if the gas can has been previously picked up and dropped.
While flashing, Survivors will have time to pick up the gas cans before they explode.
If they get destroyed, they will eventually respawn back at the location they originated.

lines.line: Tips: Overtime starts if the clock runs out while at least one survivor is holding a can. The timer flashes red and survivors have unlimited time to pour another can and extend the round, but once every can is dropped their turn is over. It can happen more than once in a round.

quoted: During a game, overtime will occur if the time limit runs out, but at least one Survivor is holding a gas can.
Overtime is indicated by the timer flashing red.

During overtime, the Survivors have an indefinite amount of time to pour another gas can into the generator and extend the time, so long as at least one Survivor is holding a gas can at all times. If all the gas cans are dropped, the Survivors' round is over.
Overtime can occur multiple times during a single round.

lines.line: Tips: Adrenaline shots speed up pouring and let a survivor keep pouring while being attacked. Bot-controlled Spitters cannot burn dropped cans in Scavenge.

quoted: Adrenaline shots speed up the pouring speed and let Survivors pour in while being attacked.
Bot-controlled Spitters cannot burn dropped cans in Scavenge.

lines.line: Summary: Infected in Scavenge are not only trying to put survivors down: stopping the pouring, and making survivors drop their cans, is what ends their turn.

quoted: In Scavenge Mode, it isn't just about incapacitating all of the Survivors. If the timer is low, preventing them from grabbing fuel with simple attacks can help end the Survivors' turn.

lines.line: Tips: Go after survivors who carry or pour cans, since any infected attack resets the pour timer. Pinning a lone pourer (pounce, tongue, charge or ride) also makes them drop the can, which matters most in overtime. A plain claw or punch only delays the pour.

quoted: Try to focus your attacks on Survivors either carrying or pouring the gas cans. Any type of attack by an Infected will reset the pour timer for a Survivor.
If a lone Survivor is pouring a gas can, pounce, pull, charge, or ride them. This will not only delay the pouring, but make them drop the can.
This is particularly important in overtime
The basic Special Infected claw or punch attack will also delay pouring (though it does not make the player drop the gas can).

lines.line: Tips: Spitter acid delays a pour without making the survivor drop the can. Spit a few seconds before they reach the generator, because the spit takes time to land and spread before it does damage.

quoted: Spitter acid will also delay a Survivor from fueling the generator (though it does not make the player drop the gas can). Make sure to spit a few seconds before they reach the generator.
it takes a short amount of time for the spit to travel and when the spit hits the ground, it takes a little bit more time to spread, before it does any damage.

lines.line: Tips: Do not spawn too eagerly once set-up ends, as the survivors may head somewhere you did not expect. Survivors who are alone and far from both the group and the generator are good targets, and enclosed can spots are good places to wait for a lone survivor.

quoted: After set-up time ends, don't be too eager to spawn. The Survivors may go to an area nowhere near where you were planning to spawn.
If there's an opportunity, go for any Survivors that are by themselves and very far away from both the rest of the Survivors and the generator, whether or not they have a gas can.
Many gas cans are enclosed and hard to reach or see from most spots. These are good areas to camp in case a lone Survivor comes by to grab a gas can.

lines.line: Summary: Scavenge survivors are told to stay near a teammate, to kill whatever is hitting them before they pour, and to take a Spitter down fast because she can destroy cans and delay the pour.

quoted: Always have at least one other Survivor near you at all times.
Don't try to pour fuel into the generator when you are being hit.
If you discover a Spitter is on the map, make sure to kill her quickly. She can destroy Gas cans and delay pouring fuel into the generator.

lines.line: Tips: Long-range weapons such as the Combat Rifle or Sniper Rifle suit the mode: there are few common infected, and distance helps against special infected that drag survivors away. If you start as survivors, go for the farthest cans first while health and supplies are good; with a weaker team or a strong infected side, take the closest first.

quoted: Use long-range weapons, such as the Combat Rifle or Sniper Rifle. There are not that many Common Infected on the maps and using a long-range weapon is better suited for killing Special Infected, especially if they can move Survivors far away from the group.

If you start the round as Survivors, go for the farthest gas cans first, while your team has very good health and supply slots are filled. However, if your team is not good and/or the Infected team is very good, go for the closest gas cans first.

lines.line: Tips: Juggling cans means tossing one forward, picking up the next and tossing that, so four or five move along at nearly running speed. Gathering several groups before heading back is much faster than one trip per group.

quoted: Instead of running with a single can in hand, you can "juggle" gas cans.
Done right, and you can juggle 4 or 5 cans at a speed only slightly less than a normal run
It is significantly faster to collect multiple groups of cans at the same time instead of running back to the generator for each group of cans.

lines.line: Tips: A Spitter can destroy a can left unattended, even briefly, forcing you through the acid to save it. Adrenaline helps in a pinch, since it speeds the pour and lets you keep pouring while you are hit.

quoted: if you leave any unattended even briefly, a Spitter may be able to spit on it, forcing you to go through the spit to save the can or let the can be destroyed.
use your Adrenaline in a pinch as you can pour gas faster and you will still pour your gas in while getting hit.

lines.line: Summary: Ambush spots for the infected on the first two chapters of The Passing, The Riverbank and The Underground. High buildings suit Hunters, and Smokers do best on whoever is last in line.

quoted: The Riverbank / The Underground / The Port

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Passing / The Riverbank
quoted: There are a few high buildings around here that you can use to pounce on a Survivor.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Passing / The Underground
quoted: Snag the last Survivor as they attempt to jump.

lines.line: Tips: The Riverbank: sneaking up behind the Bride Witch and staying there makes survivors shoot on instinct and startle her, and a survivor who comes out of one of the tents with footlockers is an easy pounce. A Smoker should pull away survivors who try to kill her, since she stands in the open.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Passing / The Riverbank
quoted: The Bride Witch is one of your greatest assets here. Sneak up behind her and stay there — the Survivors will shoot you on instinct, which will startle the Witch.
The Survivors may hide in the tents with the footlockers. Pounce on the one that comes out.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Passing / The Riverbank
quoted: The Bride Witch is out in an open area, so attempting to pull Survivors to her is out of the question. Instead, pull Survivors away that attempt to kill her

lines.line: Tips: The Underground: many high buildings help a Hunter, and a lone survivor is the target. A Smoker can pull the last survivor away from the window as the group crosses the pool hall toward the construction site. On the plank three storeys up, pull from the alley below (the common choice, so bring a distraction) or from the roof above.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Passing / The Underground
quoted: There are a lot of high buildings that you can use to your advantage.
Pounce on the loner.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Passing / The Underground
quoted: When Survivors cross the pool hall down to the construction site, pull the last Survivor away from the window.
Survivors have to cross on a plank of wood three stories above the ground.
The alleyway is the most common, so have some kind of distraction beforehand so the Survivors won't instantly target you.

lines.line: Tips: The Underground's Crescendo Event: a Hunter can pounce the furthest survivor, who is hidden by the water. A Smoker can snag the last survivor as they drop into the sewer water, and with a Hunter ready to pounce the victim after the drag it is very lethal.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Passing / The Underground
quoted: At the Crescendo Event, pounce on the furthest Survivor — you'll be hidden by the water.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Passing / The Underground
quoted: When Survivors activate the Gauntlet Crescendo, they have to drop into the sewer water again, a point of no return. Snag the last Survivor as they attempt to jump. This strategy is very lethal if you have a Hunter to pounce the victim after you snag and drag them back

lines.line: Summary: Ambush spots for the infected on the first four chapters of Hard Rain: The Milltown, The Sugar Mill, Mill Escape and Return to Town. The Sugar Mill's Witches and high ground are the main assets.

quoted: The Milltown / The Sugar Mill / Mill Escape / Return To Town / Town Escape

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Hard Rain / The Sugar Mill
quoted: The broken-down buildings offer some high vantage points.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Level Specific Strategy / Hard Rain / The Sugar Mill
quoted: Try to steer a Survivor into a Witch.

lines.line: Tips: The Milltown: houses all over the map give high pounces, especially when survivors must walk between two-storey ones. A Smoker can snare through the large hole in the Burger Tank's roof without being exposed, unless survivors climb the ladder outside, and the chapter always has an alarmed car to drag someone into.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Hard Rain / The Milltown
quoted: There are houses all over this map — use this for some high-damage pounces, especially when the Survivors are forced to walk between two-story ones.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Hard Rain / The Milltown
quoted: When entering the Burger Tank, there is a large hole in the roof that Smokers can snare Survivors from without being vulnerable (unless the Survivors climb the ladder outside to kill you).
There is always an alarmed car in this chapter.

lines.line: Tips: The Sugar Mill: catwalks, vats, broken buildings and the three-storey mill are launch points for a Hunter. In the cane field, wait for a Boomer's bile, which stops survivors seeing each other's outlines and so hides you; without a Boomer, pounce from the top of the mill. Dragging or steering a survivor into a Witch almost always incapacitates them.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Hard Rain / The Sugar Mill
quoted: There are also catwalks and vats lining the Survivors' path which serve as excellent launch points, as well as the 3-story mill itself.

Instead, wait for a Boomer shower, because this disables their ability to see the auras around their teammates, which makes you effectively invisible within the sugar cane. If there is no Boomer, then pounce from the top of the sugar mill

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Hard Rain / The Sugar Mill
quoted: Anytime you drag a Survivor into a Witch is a good drag, as it will almost certainly incapacitate them.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Level Specific Strategy / Hard Rain / The Sugar Mill
quoted: Try to steer a Survivor into a Witch. This will almost always result in a Survivor being incapacitated.

lines.line: Tips: Mill Escape and Return to Town reuse earlier spots: the Hunter's Sugar Mill tactics work in Mill Escape and its Milltown tactics work in Return to Town. In Return to Town, any rooftop or alleyway will do for a Smoker.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Hard Rain / Mill Escape
quoted: The tactics in The Sugar Mill apply here as well

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Hard Rain / Return to Town
quoted: The tactics in The Milltown apply here as well

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Hard Rain / Return to Town
quoted: Any rooftop or alleyway will do

lines.line: Summary: Ambush spots for the infected on the first four chapters of The Parish: The Waterfront, The Park, The Cemetery and The Quarter. Alarmed cars, bushes and the Cemetery's drops that cannot be climbed back up come up most.

quoted: The Waterfront / The Park / The Cemetery / The Quarter / The Bridge

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Parish / The Cemetery
quoted: The alarmed car area is the Survivors' worst nightmare.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Parish / The Cemetery
quoted: There are many "points-of-no-return" in this map

lines.line: Tips: The Waterfront: tall buildings are Hunter perches, and a Hunter can wait behind the alarmed car at the end of the level and pounce anyone who comes near. A Smoker can climb onto the kitchen's roof and grab survivors through the hole when they are inside.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Parish / The Waterfront
quoted: There are a lot of high buildings here that you can jump off of.
Hide behind the alarmed car at the end of the level and pounce anyone who comes near.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Parish / The Waterfront
quoted: There is a hole in the roof of the kitchen. Get on the roof and grab Survivors when they are in there.

lines.line: Tips: The Park: a Hunter can hide in the bushes until a survivor strays from the group, ideally with a Boomer vomiting on the pounced survivor to shield them with common infected. Pouncing the last survivor running to shut off the alarm also slows the team's rescue.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Parish / The Park
quoted: Hide in the bushes. Wait until a Survivor is separated from the rest of the group while you stand in the bushes, hidden, and then pounce on them.
This tactic works extremely well if the Boomer and the Hunter work in unison, with the Boomer vomiting on the pounced Survivor, effectively creating a shield of Common Infected.
Pounce on the last Survivor running to shut off the alarm — it'll slow the team down trying to save your victim.

lines.line: Tips: The Cemetery: a Hunter can pounce on a survivor in the dark sewers, where water covers him, or from behind a car in the alarmed car area; in the Impound Lot a Smoker can drag a survivor into a car and hope the others shoot the car, not him. The Quarter: during its Crescendo Event, drag a survivor to the ground for heavy fall damage.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Parish / The Cemetery
quoted: Pounce on a Survivor in the sewers — it's dark and vast under there, and you'll be covered by the water.
Hiding behind one of the cars and pouncing a Survivor as they come near is a good tactic here.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Parish / The Cemetery
quoted: The Impound Lot. This is the major playground for many Specials, especially the Smoker. Drag an unlucky Survivor into a car and hope that the others shoot the car and not you.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / The Parish / The Quarter
quoted: The Crescendo Event will create absolute chaos. Try dragging a Survivor down to the ground, causing them to take a lot of fall damage.
